Guangguang: Easy—and you pass Safety Theater.

stories.title: Outdoor Light Helps Eyes
stories.text:
Please listen. Guangguang Safety Theater. Episode 6. Outdoor Light Helps Eyes.

Guangguang: Mia, the outdoors called. It misses you.
Mia: Five more levels!
Guangguang: Soft outdoor light helps eyes in ways indoor screens don't.
Mia: So go outside a bit?
Guangguang: With a grown-up plan—play outside, then screens feel better too.
Mia: Outside first. Then play.
Guangguang: That's the win.

stories.title: Hot Stove, Cool Hands
stories.text:
Please listen. Guangguang Safety Theater. Episode 7. Hot Stove, Cool Hands.

Guangguang: Max, that stove is not a hand warmer.
Max: It looks shiny!
Guangguang: Hot means ouch. Cool hands stay away.
Max: So I don't touch?
Guangguang: Don't touch. Ask a grown-up. Kitchen heat is their job.
Max: Hands off. Ask first.
Guangguang: Pass Safety Theater.

stories.title: Knives Are for Grown-Ups
stories.text:
Please listen. Guangguang Safety Theater. Episode 8. Knives Are for Grown-Ups.

Guangguang: Mia, that knife is not a magic wand.
Mia: I just want to help cut!
Guangguang: Helping is great—with grown-up tools for grown-ups.
Mia: So I wait?
Guangguang: Wait. Ask. Use kid-safe helpers they give you.
Mia: Knife stays with grown-ups.
Guangguang: Safe and helpful. Pass.

stories.title: Medicine Is Not Candy
stories.text:
Please listen. Guangguang Safety Theater. Episode 9. Medicine Is Not Candy.

Guangguang: Max, those pills are not fruit snacks.
Max: But they're colorful!
Guangguang: Colorful can still be medicine. Medicine is not candy.
Max: Only if a grown-up gives it?
Guangguang: Only a trusted grown-up. Right dose, right time—never a snack raid.
Max: Not candy. Ask first.
Guangguang: Pass Safety Theater.

stories.title: Don’t Climb on Furniture
stories.text:
Please listen. Guangguang Safety Theater. Episode 10. Don’t Climb on Furniture.

Guangguang: Mia, the bookshelf is not a mountain.
Mia: I can reach the top!
Guangguang: Climbing furniture can mean a hard fall.
Mia: So ask for help instead?
Guangguang: Ask a grown-up. Feet on the floor beat flying off a chair.
Mia: No furniture mountains.
Guangguang: Smart. Pass.

stories.title: Smoke Alarm Means Go Outside
stories.text:
Please listen. Guangguang Safety Theater. Episode 11. Smoke Alarm Means Go Outside.

Guangguang: Max, that loud beep is not a game sound.
Max: It's noisy! Make it stop!
Guangguang: Smoke alarm means: get out, stay out, find a grown-up plan.
Max: Outside—not hide?
Guangguang: Outside with your grown-up. Practice the path when it's calm.
Max: Beep means go outside.
Guangguang: Pass Safety Theater.

stories.title: Stop, Look, Listen at Crossings
stories.text:
Please listen. Guangguang Safety Theater. Episode 12. Stop, Look, Listen at Crossings.

Guangguang: Mia, the street is not a race track.
Mia: I can dash!
Guangguang: At crossings: stop, look, listen.
Mia: Stop… look… listen.
Guangguang: Then go when it's safe, with a grown-up.
Mia: No dashing. Stop look listen.
Guangguang: Pass.

stories.title: Wait for the Green Light
stories.text:
Please listen. Guangguang Safety Theater. Episode 13. Wait for the Green Light.

Guangguang: Max, red means what?
Max: Go faster before it changes?
Guangguang: Nice try. Red means wait. Green means go—when clear.
Max: Wait for green.
Guangguang: Wait for the green light. Patience keeps you safe.
Max: Green light. Then walk.
Guangguang: Pass Safety Theater.

stories.title: Hold a Grown-Up’s Hand
stories.text:
Please listen. Guangguang Safety Theater. Episode 14. Hold a Grown-Up’s Hand.

Guangguang: Mia, crossing alone is not a badge of bravery.
Mia: I'm big now!
Guangguang: Big kids still hold a grown-up's hand in busy streets.
Mia: Hand hold = safe?
Guangguang: Hand hold = safe. Together beats lost.
Mia: Hold hand. Cross together.
Guangguang: Pass.

stories.title: Bike Helmet On
stories.text:
Please listen. Guangguang Safety Theater. Episode 15. Bike Helmet On.

Guangguang: Max, helmet hair is a hero look.
Max: Helmets are hot and silly!
Guangguang: Helmets protect your smart brain if you tip.
Max: So on before wheels roll?
Guangguang: Helmet on, then ride. Click it. Fit it.
Max: Helmet on. Then go.
Guangguang: Pass Safety Theater.

stories.title: Stay Where a Grown-Up Can See
stories.text:
Please listen. Guangguang Safety Theater. Episode 16. Stay Where a Grown-Up Can See.

Guangguang: Mia, hide-and-seek in a mall is a bad sequel.
Mia: I'll be right back!
Guangguang: Stay where a grown-up can see you.
Mia: In sight—not around the corner?
Guangguang: In sight. If you get separated, find a worker or stay put as you practiced.
Mia: Stay visible.
Guangguang: Pass.

stories.title: Strangers Are Not Instant Friends
stories.text:
Please listen. Guangguang Safety Theater. Episode 17. Strangers Are Not Instant Friends.

Guangguang: Max, a smile is nice. Instant best-friend? Not always.
Max: He offered candy!
Guangguang: Strangers are not instant friends. Kind can still be unknown.
Max: So I check with my grown-up?
Guangguang: Check first. Don't go. Don't take. Tell a trusted adult.
Max: Not instant friends. Ask first.
Guangguang: Pass Safety Theater.

stories.title: Say No and Find a Trusted Adult
stories.text:
Please listen. Guangguang Safety Theater. Episode 18. Say No and Find a Trusted Adult.

Guangguang: Mia, what if a plan feels wrong in your tummy?
Mia: Be polite and stay?
Guangguang: You can say no. Then find a trusted adult.
Mia: No is allowed?
Guangguang: No is allowed. Your safety comes first. Practice the words.
Mia: Say no. Find my grown-up.
Guangguang: Pass.

stories.title: Passwords Stay Private
stories.text:
Please listen. Guangguang Safety Theater. Episode 19. Passwords Stay Private.

Guangguang: Max, is your password a secret or a billboard?
Max: I told my classmate so we can share!
Guangguang: Passwords stay private. Sharing can unlock your stuff for others.
Max: Even friends?
Guangguang: Even friends. Grown-ups help if you forget—not the whole class.
Max: Password private.
Guangguang: Pass Safety Theater.

stories.title: Ask Before Clicking Links
stories.text:
Please listen. Guangguang Safety Theater. Episode 20. Ask Before Clicking Links.

Guangguang: Mia, that shiny button says FREE PRIZE.
Mia: Tap tap!
Guangguang: Ask before clicking links. Some links are tricks.
Mia: Ask a grown-up first?
Guangguang: Ask first. If it feels rushy or weird, pause.
Mia: No surprise taps. Ask.
Guangguang: Pass.

stories.title: Wash Hands Before Eating
stories.text:
Please listen. Guangguang Safety Theater. Episode 21. Wash Hands Before Eating.

Guangguang: Max, your hands visited the playground, then the sandwich?
Max: I'm starving!
Guangguang: Wash hands before eating. Soap beats invisible germ hitchhikers.
Max: Soap, rinse, then food?
Guangguang: Soap, rinse, then food. Quick and powerful.
Max: Wash first. Eat second.
Guangguang: Pass Safety Theater.

stories.title: Swim Only With a Grown-Up
stories.text:
Please listen. Guangguang Safety Theater. Episode 22. Swim Only With a Grown-Up.

Guangguang: Mia, water is fun—and deep.
Mia: I can doggy-paddle!
Guangguang: Swim only with a grown-up watching. Water rules are not optional.
Mia: No solo swimming?
Guangguang: No solo. Grown-up eyes on. Life jackets when they say so.
Mia: Grown-up with me.
Guangguang: Pass.

stories.title: Wear Sunscreen Outside
stories.text:
Please listen. Guangguang Safety Theater. Episode 23. Wear Sunscreen Outside.

Guangguang: Max, the sun is strong even when you feel fine.
Max: Sunscreen is sticky!
Guangguang: Wear sunscreen outside. Sticky now beats burn later.
Max: Put it on before play?
Guangguang: Before play. Grown-ups help with face and ears.
Max: Sunscreen on. Then run.
Guangguang: Pass Safety Theater.

stories.title: Tell an Adult If Something Hurts
stories.text:
Please listen. Guangguang Safety Theater. Episode 24. Tell an Adult If Something Hurts.

Guangguang: Mia, brave is not silent when something hurts.
Mia: I don't want to bother anyone.
Guangguang: Tell an adult if something hurts—body or feelings.
Mia: Saying it is okay?
Guangguang: Saying it helps them help you. Early words beat big worries.
Mia: If it hurts, I tell.
Guangguang: Pass. You're Safety Theater strong.
